newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Court suspends Russian Rosgosstrakh privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Court suspends Russian Rosgosstrakh privatisation.

text.p: The Moscow Arbitration Court has suspended privatisation of Russia's biggest insurer Rosgosstrakh pending a suit from the union of depositors at state savings bank Sberbank, a Rosgosstrakh spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
The court ruled that privatisation of Rosgosstrakh should be suspended until the court takes a final decision on March 25, Irina Aristova told Reuters.

The union filed a suit against the State Property Committee, which is responsible for privatisation in Russia, asking for the sale of Rosgosstrakh to be suspended as the company owns about 24 billion roubles ($4.2 million) in 1992 prices to its depositors, she said.
The debt represents money Rosgosstrakh collected before the start of economic reforms in 1992, when it was the only insurance company for households.
Aristova said Rosgosstrakh had about 52.5 million contracts with individuals at that time.
She said a 1995 law and 1996 presidential decree had transformed Rosgosstrakh and Sberbank debts to individuals into state debt.
"Our charter says we are not responsible for state debt," she said.
Under Rossgosstrakh's privatisation plan its employees had subscribed for 20 percent of shares and have a priority right for a further 30 percent.
The remaining 50 percent will be sold at a cash auction.
The government's Audit Chamber is reviewing Rosgosstrakh's privatisation plan and the State Duma lower house of parliament asked the chamber to report its results by March 10.
